paragraphs.text: A cake of [Yunnan white](yunnan-white:definition) from Yunnan, made from the province's large-leaf tea plants rather than the smaller bush cultivars of Fujian. Like all [white tea](white:definition), it is made in the fewest steps. The leaf is never heated to stop its change and never rolled, so it keeps its natural shape.

The Yunnan way differs from the Fujian one. The leaf is [withered indoors or in shade](yunnan-white:making) instead of under the midday sun, then dried by air, without the final low bake that Fujian white usually gets. It was then pressed into a cake, one of the shapes Yunnan borrows from pu'er. White tea from Yunnan has only found its place in the market in recent years, though [local practice may be older](yunnan-white:history).

brewing.text: Yunnan white is brewed gently, as a white tea is, in a gaiwan or small pot, and it gives many infusions; the leaf holds up well.

notice.text: A honeyed, sweet cup, often richer and fuller than Fujian white, with little bitterness, sometimes fruit like apricot or melon and a hay or herbal note. Yabao is sweet and silky, often with pine or herbal notes.
